subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Boundary Placement, Parallel vs Waterfall Fetching, Suspense and Error Boundaries, useTransition/startTransition, Suspense in RSC and Next.js App Router, React 19 use hook, Common Anti-Patterns, Verification) and current React/Next.js docs (react.dev Suspense/use/useTransition, Next.js loading-ui-and-streaming, useSearchParams).

cases.scenario: A static Next.js dashboard has a fast header, a slow chart, a slow recommendations panel, and a Client Component search bar that calls `useSearchParams()`.
cases.context: The product wants initial HTML for the fast shell, independent reveal for the two slow widgets, and no full-page client-rendering bailout from search params.
cases.question: Place the Suspense boundaries and name the failure mode each boundary prevents.
expected_flags: Keep the fast header outside slow widget Suspense boundaries so it can render immediately.
Give the slow chart and slow recommendations panel separate feature-level Suspense boundaries so they reveal independently.
Wrap the smallest Client subtree that calls `useSearchParams()` in Suspense to avoid bailing the whole static route into client rendering.
expected_fix_hints: Use skeletons that preserve the chart and recommendations panel dimensions.
Start independent data dependencies as siblings or pass Promises down instead of awaiting parent data first.
Pair each loading boundary with an error boundary where failure should replace the same subtree.
absent_signals: Do not put one root Suspense boundary around the whole dashboard.
Do not assume `useSearchParams()` is harmless in production static builds without Suspense.
Do not duplicate Suspense behavior with per-widget `isLoading` flags unless the data source is not Suspense-enabled.

cases.scenario: A route segment has a segment-local loading file, but users still see no fallback while the same segment's layout waits for runtime user data.
cases.context: The team assumed the segment loading file covers everything in the segment.
cases.question: Explain why the fallback does not cover the layout wait and propose the smallest structural fix.
expected_flags: A segment loading file creates an implicit Suspense boundary around the page and nested children below it.
The same segment's layout, template, and error file sit outside that implicit boundary.
Runtime layout data needs to move into the page/subtree or be wrapped by an explicit Suspense boundary at the desired layout location.
expected_fix_hints: Move the slow user-specific fetch from the layout into the page or a child subtree when the layout shell should render first.
Add an explicit Suspense boundary around the runtime layout region if the layout must own the data.
Keep route-level loading UI only for waits it actually owns.
absent_signals: Do not claim that adding or renaming the segment loading file alone fixes layout-owned waits.
Do not move the whole application layout under one boundary.
Do not route this primarily to server-components-design unless the question is what should run as a Server Component.

cases.scenario: A profile page renders a ProfileHeader from `await fetchUser()`, then a child ActivityFeed that calls `await fetchActivity(userId)`. The page feels slow even though both queries are individually fast.
cases.context: fetchActivity only needs the userId, which is a route param already available; it does not need the full user object.
cases.question: Diagnose the latency and restructure the fetching.
expected_flags: Identify a waterfall: the child's fetch only starts after the parent's await resolves, sequentializing two requests that could run together.
Kick off both independent fetches at the same level of the tree (e.g. start both Promises, then Promise.all) — or pass Promises down.
Where each section can stream independently, wrap each in its own Suspense boundary instead of awaiting both before render.
Note that tree depth correlates with waterfall risk; flat sibling fetches stream optimally.
expected_fix_hints: Start fetchActivity from the route param in parallel with fetchUser instead of inside the awaited child.
Use Promise.all when both values are needed before render, or separate Suspense boundaries when they can reveal independently.
absent_signals: Do not add a Suspense boundary and assume it removes the waterfall — Suspense alone does not parallelize fetches.
Do not keep the child awaiting data it could have started earlier.

cases.scenario: A tabbed settings panel wraps each tab's content (which suspends on a Suspense-enabled fetch) in a single Suspense boundary. Every tab click flashes the skeleton even though the previous tab was fully rendered.
cases.context: The team wants the previous tab to stay visible during the load and a subtle pending indicator on the active tab button.
cases.question: How should the agent stop the fallback flicker on tab switches?
expected_flags: Wrap the state update that switches tabs in startTransition (via useTransition) so the update is non-urgent.
React then keeps the previous tab's committed render visible while the new tab's data loads instead of unmounting to the fallback.
Use the isPending flag from useTransition to show a subtle pending state on the tab control.
The fallback should still show on first render (no prior committed content to preserve).
expected_fix_hints: Drive the active-tab pending UI from isPending, not from a manual isLoading flag.
absent_signals: Do not wrap the initial-load update in startTransition expecting it to keep (nonexistent) previous content.
Do not add a manual isLoading flag alongside the Suspense boundary to suppress the flicker.

Surfaces this expected flag: Use the isPending flag from useTransition to show a subtle pending state on the tab control.

cases.scenario: A widget that streams in via `use(dataPromise)` inside a Suspense boundary throws when the fetch rejects. The whole page crashes with an unhandled error instead of showing an error UI for just that widget.
cases.context: The product wants a failed widget to show an inline error message while sibling widgets keep streaming in.
cases.question: How should the agent make the failure recoverable without affecting siblings?
expected_flags: Add an error boundary as a DISTINCT component from the Suspense boundary — Suspense catches suspension, the error boundary catches thrown Errors.
Nest ErrorBoundary outside Suspense for this widget so a failure replaces the loading state of that subtree cleanly.
Scope the ErrorBoundary+Suspense pair to the single widget so sibling widgets under their own boundaries keep streaming.
React has no built-in function-component ErrorBoundary (as of React 19) — use react-error-boundary or a class component; Server Component errors are caught by Next.js error.tsx.
expected_fix_hints: Keep each widget's boundary pair independent so one failure does not unmount the others.
absent_signals: Do not try to make the Suspense boundary itself catch the thrown error.
Do not put a single page-level error boundary that would replace all widgets on one widget's failure.

cases.scenario: A user asks whether a component should be a Server Component or Client Component, and whether the page should use SSR, SSG, or CSR.
cases.context: The prompt mentions loading states, but the unresolved decision is execution location and rendering strategy, not boundary placement.
cases.question: Should suspense-patterns own the request?
expected_flags: The primary owners are server-components-design for Server vs Client Component placement and rendering-models for SSR/SSG/CSR strategy.
suspense-patterns becomes relevant only after the tree and rendering strategy are chosen and the loading/reveal boundaries need design.
The response should preserve the distinction between rendering strategy, server/client split, and Suspense boundary placement.
expected_fix_hints: Route first to server-components-design or rendering-models based on the user's actual decision.
Return to suspense-patterns when deciding which subtree waits, which fallback renders, and how streaming chunks reveal.
Name Suspense as an in-tree mechanism, not the owner of the rendering-strategy choice.
absent_signals: Do not treat every React performance or rendering question as Suspense boundary work.
Do not answer Server Component ownership with only loading-boundary advice.
Do not collapse SSR/SSG/CSR selection into Suspense placement.
